About sheet: Recommended Citation: "Global Energy Monitor, Global Integrated Power Tracker, September 2026 release."

Rows: 183,404 units in "Power facilities"; Types kept: wind, utility-scale solar, hydropower, geothermal, bioenergy (solar thermal is a Technology of utility-scale solar, so it is included). 101,731 plants (GEM location ID) with an operating renewable unit; their renewable units' Capacity (MW) summed per plant.

Threshold (ruling R25): plants with coordinates and no TransitionZero unit at each step tried, up to the 5,000 markers a layer draws: 100 MW: 9,047 plants; 150 MW: 5,379 plants; 200 MW: 4,021 plants. Kept at 200 MW.
7 kept plants also have operating units of other fuels (not counted here; the Power plants layer counts all fuels).
The Power plants layer shows all fuels at 500 MW or more, so a large renewable plant is in both layers when both are on.

Ruling R22: the About sheet says records with a "TZ ID" in Other IDs (unit/phase) come partly or wholly from TransitionZero's Solar Asset Mapper (August 2025), CC BY-NC 4.0. Non-commercial data is never bundled (C6), so a plant with any such unit is left out whole: 18,723 plants with operating units, 0 of them 200 MW or more (listed under dropped).

A plant's position is its first operating unit's Latitude and Longitude; 418 kept plants have units more than 0.05 degrees apart. A plant's type is its largest Type by capacity (0 kept plants have more than one; see the types column), and its country the Country/area with the most capacity (0 span two).
Country/area names map to ISO3 through the workbook's own "Regions, area, and countries" sheet (ISO-alpha3 Code), then the app's country names.
Check: kept plants by largest Type: wind 1,429; utility-scale solar 1,271; hydropower 1,265; bioenergy 41; geothermal 14.

Check: largest plants: Three Gorges Dam hydroelectric plant (CHN, hydropower) 22,500 MW; Baihetan hydroelectric plant (CHN, hydropower) 16,000 MW; Itaipu hydroelectric plant (BRA, hydropower) 14,000 MW; Xiluodu hydroelectric plant (CHN, hydropower) 13,860 MW; Belo Monte hydroelectric plant (BRA, hydropower) 11,233 MW.
Published: GEM names the release month only; 2026-09-01 stands for September 2026 and is never shown as a day.
